note: Each case is a command with an expected outcome. `verify-beta.mjs` runs them and records exit code, pass/fail, and evidence kind. `kind` distinguishes a real host check from a service-level test: a service test passing does NOT imply the host mounts the plugin, and a route answering HTTP 200 does NOT imply the feature works.

cases.expected: exit 0 and host-modules.json lists the platform modules with versions
cases.why: The release is a host extension: without the host's platform modules nothing else can run. This must fail loudly when no host install is found, never fall back to a developer store.

cases.expected: exit 0; tools/mermaid and tools/ts-toolchain installed from their own lockfiles
cases.why: Mermaid and TypeScript are pinned in two separate tool closures with their own package-lock.json; the root install does not cover them.

cases.expected: exit 0 and the generated offline runtime matches the committed source
cases.why: The offline report runtime is a generated artifact with a pinned CSP hash. The original workspace shipped a stale copy, which is exactly the failure this check exists to catch.

cases.expected: exit 0; module-table banner, factory footer and external contract all pass
cases.why: The client bundle is loaded through the DSH module table. A wrong banner id or a missing external breaks the host UI while the build still 'succeeds'.

cases.expected: exit 0 and packages/evolver-ui/lib/index.js is written
cases.why: The package's `main` points at lib/index.js; without it the Loader entry cannot import and the client scanner never sees the dsh.client declaration.

cases.expected: exit 0 under strict mode
cases.why: The backend is the bulk of the product. It typechecks against the vendored platform declarations, which are the type pin (the published @deepseek-ai packages do not reproduce the host's Events interface).

cases.expected: exit 0 under strict mode
cases.why: The build scripts are part of the release closure; an untypechecked script is an unverified build step.

cases.expected: all three exit 0
cases.why: Three strict product subconfigurations, in addition to the full UI root check.

cases.expected: exit 0; report the actual pass/fail/skip counts (do not hard-code 73)
cases.why: Six related suites cover external results, metrics, packages, takeover, takeover adoption and wiki workspaces. These are the domain regression baseline.

cases.expected: exit 0; report the actual pass/fail/skip counts
cases.why: Covers the research cycle host/team adapters, general reports (including the offline runtime), paper commands and the paper library. These are service-level tests: they do NOT prove the host mounts anything.

cases.expected: exit 0; the profile patch gains the six evolver entries with their config blocks
cases.why: The overlay must be generated from the tree's real location and must carry the config; an entry without config fails activation.

cases.expected: the host prints its URL and logs NO 'entries did not activate' warning
cases.why: This is the only check that proves the plugin actually loads in a real DSH host. A silent activation failure still serves the web UI, so the warning line is the signal.

cases.expected: HTTP 200 with a JSON body naming the service and the resolved artifact roots
cases.why: Proves the workbench route is mounted AND that repo-relative config resolved against the repository rather than the process working directory.

cases.expected: HTTP 403 with SCOPE_DENIED
cases.why: A read route that answers 200 without a grant would be a security regression. The fence must be observed, not assumed.

cases.expected: HTTP 400 with SESSION_REQUIRED
cases.why: Proves both routes are mounted (an unmounted route returns 404) while still refusing to serve without an owner session.

cases.command: grep for F:/, F:\\, G:\\Anaconda, C:\\Users in the release tree (excluding node_modules and build output)
cases.expected: no hits in shipped source, config, scripts or fixtures
cases.why: The whole point of the cleanup. A hit is either a real leak or an explanatory comment; the check reports them so a human decides which.

cases.expected: exit 0; the frozen phase2 manifest carries no machine-local sourceUri
cases.why: The frozen manifest ships as-is (its digests need the source git history to re-derive), so its one machine-local field is rewritten rather than silently dropped.

cases.expected: every path in verification/release-files.json exists with the recorded SHA-256
cases.why: Proves the delivered tree matches the recorded snapshot.
